name: Viatris

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Viatris.svg, hosted on commons.wikimedia.org)

description: Viatris makes and sells prescription medicines in more than 165 countries, formed in 2020 from Mylan (generics) and Pfizer's off-patent Upjohn brands. Despite the 'generic drugs' reputation, 64% of its FY2025 net sales came from brands (Lipitor, Norvasc, Lyrica, EpiPen, Viagra, Creon) that lost patent protection but keep selling; only 36% came from generics. It is organised by geography, not by product: Developed Markets (US and Europe) is 60% of revenue, Greater China 16%, Japan-Australia-New Zealand 8%, Emerging Markets 16%. Customers are a small number of very large US wholesalers, pharmacy chains and payors, plus government-run reimbursement systems abroad, so price pressure and government volume-based procurement (China) matter more than launches. Recent troubles: a $2.94B goodwill write-down in Q1 2025 and FDA import restrictions on its Indore, India plant.

businessLines.name: Developed Markets
businessLines.how: Sells branded off-patent and generic prescription drugs to a small number of very large US wholesalers, pharmacy chains and payors, and to European health systems that regulate prices; revenue is per unit sold at negotiated or government-set prices, helped by new complex-product launches (iron sucrose, octreotide injectable, and others).
businessLines.description: North America (mainly the US) and Europe. Significant products: Lyrica, Lipitor, Creon, Breyna, Influvac, Wixela Inhub, EpiPen Auto-Injector, Fraxiparine, Yupelri. Brands $4,571.2M and generics $3,942.8M of segment net sales in FY2025.

businessLines.name: Greater China
businessLines.how: Sells off-patent Pfizer-heritage brands through hospitals, and increasingly retail pharmacy and e-commerce; the government's volume-based procurement (VBP) programme, now covering about 490 molecules including all major Viatris brands, squeezes hospital price and volume.
businessLines.description: Mainland China, Taiwan and Hong Kong; portfolio is predominantly branded loss-of-exclusivity products (Lipitor, Norvasc, Viagra). Brands $2,321.8M, generics $10.7M.

revenue.note: FY2024 $2,167.8M total revenues; net sales $2,332.5M vs $2,166.5M

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $2,167.8M total revenues; net sales $2,332.5M vs $2,166.5M

businessLines.name: JANZ (Japan, Australia, New Zealand)
businessLines.how: Sells mainly through wholesalers at government-regulated reimbursement prices in Japan, and through the wholesale system in Australia under the pharmaceutical benefits scheme.
businessLines.description: Japan (sold through wholesalers to doctors, hospitals and pharmacies under National Health Insurance pricing), Australia (pharmaceutical benefits scheme). Significant products: Amitiza, Effexor, Lipacreon, Lyrica, EpiPen. Brands $617.4M, generics $576.4M.

businessLines.name: Emerging Markets
businessLines.how: Sells brands and generics in more than 125 developing-market countries, including the ARV (HIV antiretroviral) franchise; the ARV business was hurt in 2025 by supply disruption tied to the Indore plant (10-K).
businessLines.description: More than 125 developing-market countries in Asia, Africa, Eastern Europe, Latin America and the Middle East, plus the ARV (HIV antiretroviral) franchise. Brands $1,673.6M, generics $536.5M.

whatsNext.text: FDA reinspection of the Indore, India oral finished-dose plant, expected to be ready in 2026; import alert on 11 products stays until the warning letter is lifted
Nashik, India plant: production resumed after the February 2026 fire, but May 2026 FDA Form 483 observations and remediation are expected to affect product supply in the second half of 2026
